chapter: Russell's band, records and Armstrong in the studio
title: Listening to 'Tight Like That' with Red Allen, Barbarin's chimes and Metcalf's vocal
summary: He identifies Red Allen's solos and Metcalf as vocalist, who contributed the lyrics though no longer in the band.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Now, "It's Tight Like That," the title, that must have been an expression.
Yeah...
[PAUSE: TELEPHONE]
[MUSIC PLAYS]
The band had changed now, because now you've got Pops Foster on bass...
Well, he had (?) in the band ....(?)....
[DURING TRUMPET SOLO] That's Red Allen. [THEN DURING CHORUS, A LEAD VOCAL]...
That's Metcalf.
Metcalf. [ANOTHER RED ALLEN TRUMPET SOLO] [AS MUSIC ENDS...] I had forgotten all about that recording. Yeah, I forgot all about that.
Now, there it appears, at the end, that there's piano as well as chimes going at the same time.

Well, I wasn't paying particular attention. But it could have been that after the piano finished, then you hear maybe the chimes. Maybe he just picked up and hit the chord. Maybe. I wasn't paying attention to when the chimes were. Maybe that was Paul Barbarin...
On the chimes.
...on the chimes.
I think so.
Because he had chimes of his own. He had bells or whatever they called them that he used to it. He used to play 'em pretty good, too.
Yeah, I think it must have been Barbarin, because they were too much together.
Yeah. I wasn't particularly paying attention to it.
Metcalf told me when I played it for him once, that although he was out of the band, Russell called him up because he said, 'We're going to record your number.'
That's possible, yeah.
And he came down, and he didn't bring his horn, but he was just there to do the vocals.
Yeah.
The vocalists on that are Henry Allen, J.C. Higgenbotham and Louis Metcalf.
Louis Metcalf, yeah.
You can clearly hear him on there.
Well, it's his... They're his lyrics. You know what I mean?! Heh-heh. Yeah, they are his lyrics. He contributed sayings and things to a lot of little numbers
that didn't stay in the book. Because he was a fun guy, you know. He was always sittin' on the bandstand playin'. I mean, you know, crackin' jokes and one thing or another. Yeah, he loved fun.
